definitions.explanation: Describes doing something because there is no other option, even though one would prefer not to. Emphasizes that the action is taken out of necessity rather than desire.

examples.japanese: やむなく⟦{中止|ちゅうし}した→中止する：21909_chuushisuru⟧。
examples.english: We had no choice but to cancel.

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まり→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧、やむなく⟦タクシー→タクシー：00816_takushii⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: The trains stopped, so I reluctantly took a taxi home.

examples.japanese: ⟦{予算|よさん}→予算：03663_yosan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{都合|つごう}→都合：01672_tsugou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、やむなく⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{縮小|しゅくしょう}する→縮小する：25359_shukushousuru⟧ことになった。
examples.english: Due to budget constraints, we had no choice but to scale back the plan.

notes:
An adverbial form derived from ⟦{止|や}む→止む：01153_yamu⟧なし (unavoidable), itself from the verb ⟦{止|や}む→止む：01153_yamu⟧ (to cease, to stop). Conveys that the speaker or subject acts only because circumstances leave no alternative.

USAGE:
Used in both spoken and written Japanese, though it has a slightly formal or stiff quality. Common in news reports, business communication, and narrative writing. In casual speech, しかたなく or しょう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧ are more natural.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- やむなく⟦{中止|ちゅうし}する→中止する：21909_chuushisuru⟧ — to cancel unavoidably
- やむなく⟦{断念|だんねん}する→断念する：20717_dannensuru⟧ — to reluctantly give up
- やむなく⟦{辞退|じたい}する→辞退する：18992_jitaisuru⟧ — to withdraw reluctantly
- やむなく⟦{同意|どうい}する→同意する：06056_douisuru⟧ — to agree reluctantly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しかたなく — reluctantly; more casual and conversational
- しょう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧ — reluctantly; casual, often implies mild resignation
- ⟦やむを{得|え}ず→やむを得ず：08528_yamuwoezu⟧ — unavoidably; more formal written variant with the same meaning
